Module 3: Google Docs

Write, format, structure, review, and send professional documents in Google Docs: notices, handbooks, updates, and letters.

5
Lessons
120
Minutes
5
Practice simulations
Beginner
Level

What You'll Learn

  • How to start documents from blank pages and templates and format text, paragraphs, and lists
  • How to structure long documents with headings, the tabs and outlines panel, a table of contents, headers, footers, page numbers, and page setup
  • How to add tables, images, smart chips, and building blocks, and how to use voice typing
  • How to review with comments, assignments, Suggesting mode, and version history
  • How to proofread, print, download, email, and copy a finished document

Real-World Scenario

Parkview's documents are the office's voice: the water shutoff notice on the lobby board, the tenant handbook every new resident receives, the weekly maintenance update, the new pet policy, and the welcome letter for each move-in. You write and finish them all in Google Docs, working with Denise, Marcus, Kim, and Priya in the same files instead of emailing drafts back and forth.

Lessons

Complete each lesson in order. Watch the slideshow, read the notes, try the practice simulation, and finish the challenge.

Lesson 1⏱ 25 min
📝

Creating and Formatting Documents

Start a document, then format text and paragraphs with the toolbar: fonts and sizes, bold and color, alignment, lists and checklists, line spacing, and paint format.

Lesson 2⏱ 25 min
📝

Headings, the Outline, and Page Setup

Give a long document real structure with paragraph styles, move around it with tabs and outlines, add a table of contents, headers, footers, page numbers, and breaks, and choose pages or pageless.

Lesson 3⏱ 25 min
📝

Tables, Images, Smart Chips, and Voice Typing

Add tables and images, insert smart chips for people, dates, and files, drop in building blocks like meeting notes, and dictate with voice typing.

Lesson 4⏱ 25 min
📝

Comments, Suggestions, and Version History

Review documents with your team: comment, reply, and assign tasks, suggest edits instead of making them, accept or reject suggestions, and name and restore versions.

Lesson 5⏱ 20 min
📝

Proofreading, Printing, and Sending Documents

Finish a document the professional way: check spelling and grammar, use word count and find and replace, then print, download, email, or copy it.
